correctness.rationale: For all real \(A>0\), \(\omega>0\), and \(\rho=A\omega>1\), the normalized fixed-point equation \(u=\sin(\rho u-\theta)\) yields multiplier squared \(\rho^2(1-u^2)\), so strict sinks have \(|u|>\sqrt{1-\rho^{-2}}\). Two inverse-phase parametrizations are strictly monotone and join only at \(u=1\), covering a single open arc of half-width \(h=\arcsin(1/\rho)\) about \(c=\sqrt{\rho^2-1}-\pi/2\) for positive sinks. Reflection gives negative sinks. Circular-arc overlap and \(c=j\pi\) at the resonant parameter sequence prove all remaining results. Endpoints with unit-modulus multipliers are excluded; 389 independent finite consistency assertions agreed with the theorem.
